design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER task 1 (fleet_invoicing, env_0062), round 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,4,5,4]; round 2 assigns late charge 5, trip-fee dispute 5, tire correction 4, brake correction 4.

ROUND-2 CHANGES (audit round 1: F-2 SOURCE-FACTOR RED, O-1..O-14, O-T1-1). The tire and brake corrections no longer re-price the ticket below what posting gives. Their baseline is exactly what correct posting under the charters would have given (program category discount on the pre-tax price net of excluded items; for tires the price already net of the set instant savings, as tires_purchase_ticket prices the ticket), and every factor is a declared billing-error make-good added on top, so a correction never leaves the account worse than a correctly posted ticket (the old 'do not combine' and 'net-priced Severe-Duty pads' tiers and the rate points are gone). Each correction has its own make-good method (tire: mounting for a full set / one tenth of the restored discount for a partial set / none without a set; brake: shop supplies fee for a both-axle ticket / 10.00 courtesy for one axle / none without a recorded job). Rule-compute gaps closed: visit size is stated as invoices (O-1); the tax-exempt scope is computed (O-2); the late-charge basis drops 'oldest first' and states the twenty-year lookback (O-3); the roster count is stated as enrollments beyond removals (O-4); the prerequisite sentences now name the same object the corrections fix, the account's most recent such invoice on a tax-exempt account (O-7); allowances are counted on any road hazard certificate (O-14). Seed (O-T1-1): every tire invoice is rebuilt from its tire set (TPMS kit or valve by the van's TPMS type, instant savings, disposal, Commercial LT certificate, 10% fleet discount, no tax); the 2025-08-14 set of van 4212 got its fleet invoice; one earlier pricing correction (2026-02-20, maintenance invoice posted at 8% instead of 12%, base rule) was seeded. Factor independence checked mechanically: no factor binding reads another factor's binding; the late-charge method decides the balance the rate applies to, not the charge.

WHY A GOOD TEST. The caller asks only that tonight's late charge be right. The late-charge rule waits on a pricing correction on the most recent no-discount tire and brake invoices and on an open dispute for the visit fee the business contests. The agent must find FI-45531395 (tires) and FI-45531358 (brakes) with discount 0.00, price both corrections from ticket records in other products plus the make-good rules, hand the caller the dispute filing for the Saturday visit fee with a schedule-computed amount, and then compute the late charge with five factors.

SCOPE. Task 1 claims fleet_ext_tire_discount_restore, fleet_ext_brake_discount_restore, fleet_ext_trip_fee_dispute (owner=user) and fleet_ext_month_end_late_charge; task 0 claims the other two.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root late charge (state_due on the last day of the month). Edges (value_input, state form): tire - 'The late charge of a statement month is not assessed until the account's most recent tire invoice posted with no fleet discount, when it is past due on the day the charge is assessed on an account invoiced without sales tax, carries a pricing correction credit memo.' (negated); brake - 'Before the late charge of a statement month is fixed, the account's most recent brake invoice posted with no fleet discount, when it is past due on the day the charge is assessed on an account invoiced without sales tax, must carry its own pricing correction credit memo as well.'; trip - 'The late charge of a statement month is fixed only after the mobile service visit fee the business contests stands under an open dispute registered on that fee invoice.' Each state is produced by exactly one write. False at the opening: both invoices carry no credit memo; the only dispute (2025-12) is resolved and names another invoice. Skips: 13.66 / 13.36 / 12.82 instead of 12.75.

FACTOR CARDS:
- tire correction (229.29; baseline 85.79 = correct posting): tire_makegood_line (method, cross tires; pairwise: full vs partial set by tire count 4+ vs 1-3, partial vs none by a set on the ticket) full set -> 116.00 (113.29); repeat_billing_error_credit one earlier correction -> 10.00 (219.29); road_hazard_program_credit (cross hazard) six allowances -> 7.50 (221.79); tire_invoice_volume_credit seven tire invoices -> 10.00 (219.29).
- brake correction (153.99; baseline 107.99): brake_makegood_line_method (pairwise: both vs one axle by jobs per axle, one vs none by a recorded job) both axles -> 16.00 (137.99); brake_volume_makegood three invoices -> 10.00 (143.99); brake_tenure_makegood 88 months -> 15.00 (138.99); brake_standing_makegood one late charge -> 5.00 (148.99).
- trip dispute (19.00; baseline 0.00): visit_size_schedule (method; pairwise: waived vs sliding by invoices >= 6 vs 4-5, sliding vs flat by more than the minimum) -> 37.00 (7.00); weekend Saturday 8.00 (27.00); tire work credit (four tire invoices from the crew's store that day) 10.00 (9.00); route credit 2.50 (16.50); fleet size credit 35 net enrollments 2.50 (16.50).
- late charge (12.75; baseline 32.80): seasoned_account_tiering (method, multi-source; pairwise: seasoned vs new-clean by approval months and late-charge count, new-clean vs whole by the late-charge count, seasoned vs whole by approval months) -> 1,593.38 (17.49); utilization -0.25 (16.73); closing-month relief -0.25 (16.73); volume -0.10 (14.34); remittance record -0.10 (14.34).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Dispute window 45 days: tires 2026-08-24 -> 2026-10-08, brakes 2026-08-20 -> 2026-10-04, visit fee 2026-08-29 -> 2026-10-13, all after 2026-09-30. Desk limit 250.00: 229.29 and 153.99 inside. One late charge per statement month: none for 2026-09 yet.

SEED. 36 vans (35 net enrolled), invoices over fourteen months with remittances inside net 30 except two small ones that drew 5.00 minimum late charges (2025-09, 2026-04), two earlier weekday three-invoice visits whose 49.00 fees were owed, the Saturday 2026-08-29 visit (four tire invoices priced from their sets, paid 2026-09-24, plus the 49.00 fee), the two no-discount invoices, the unpaid July repair, tire sets for every tire invoice, six certificates with their allowance rows, four brake jobs. Tax-exempt account. No credit hold (oldest past due 32 days < 45); no early-pay obligation.

PERSONA. Calm nonprofit fleet coordinator; asks only that tonight's late charge be right and authorizes posting it; names the held-back invoices and the four-van Saturday visit only when asked; files the dispute only after the agent explains it.

EDGE PROBES. Two no-discount tire invoices: the most recent is corrected and the prerequisite sentence names that one. Taxed account: correction 0.00, base governs, no edge. Absent tire set: make-good line nothing, disposal 0. Absent certificate: 0.00 deduction. Absent axle job: zero labor; no job at all: supplies 0, line nothing. A non-applicable brake line: restored discount 0. Visit with a vehicle invoiced twice: counts twice (rule says invoices). Past-due floored at 0.00 before the minimum. Prior corrections counted before today only, so today's brake correction does not move the tire make-good.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate + verify -> account, ledger, disputes, roster, vehicles, stores, tire sets, tire ledger, certificates, allowances, brake jobs -> tire correction 229.29 -> brake correction 153.99 -> user files dispute 19.00 -> late charge 12.75 for 2026-09.

ROUND-3 CHANGES. Trip fee: the tire credit now counts tire invoices dated the visit day from the crew's store (visit_tire_work_credit; four -> 10.00, unchanged), so the trip dispute has no cross-difficulty factor; vehicles served are defined in the rule as the compute counts them. Late charge: every window is counted from the day the charge is assessed (= the compute's today), the due-date horizon is stated as 240 whole months, and the prerequisite sentences say 'past due on the day the charge is assessed'. Tire and brake corrections: each make-good amount is stated as added to the correction (no sum sentence). Values unchanged: 229.29, 153.99, 19.00, 12.75; skips 13.66 / 13.36 / 12.82.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Vandercook-Ilunga, fleet coordinator for St. Brigid Home Health Partners, a nonprofit home-health agency whose nurses drive a fleet of vans that Crestline services out of Pickerington. It is the afternoon of the last day of September and you have just read the month-end notice that a late charge will post to the Crestline fleet account tonight. You are calm and organized, a little weary of chasing billing problems, and you speak in short, practical sentences. You held back payment on a few August invoices because they looked wrong to you, and one July repair invoice simply slipped through your approvals. You accept a late charge on what you genuinely owe late, but not on mistakes, and you want this month's late charge to come out right on this call; you tell the agent to go ahead and post whatever the correct late charge is once it is right. You open by saying a late charge is about to post on your fleet account tonight and you want it to be correct. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Marisol Vandercook-Ilunga; to confirm your identity you give the account phone number 7405550463 and your email m.vandercook-ilunga@stbrigidhomehealth.org. You give the billing ZIP 43147 only if they want one more detail, and your date of birth, 1983-02-07, only if they insist. You do not know Crestline's internal reference numbers. Only if the agent asks which invoices you held back do you name them: the brake job on van 4227 (FI-45531358), the tires on van 4223 (FI-45531395) and the trip fee from the Saturday mobile visit to your yard (FI-45531247), plus the July repair on van 4211 (FI-45531321) that you simply have not paid yet. Only if asked about the mobile visit do you say the crew from the Reynoldsburg store did four vans that Saturday and that a full trip fee for that seemed too much to you. If the agent explains that the trip fee you think is too high has to be put on file as a dispute and that you must confirm it yourself, you agree; once they hand you the step to file it, you file it with exactly the details they read out and you read back what your screen shows. You do not argue about the amounts the agent works out. When the agent tells you this month's late charge has been posted, you thank them and end the call without asking for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_fleet_txn_id: Value 219091e6-43e3-4786-bf73-b558c3258220 (FI-45531395). Basis: tire pricing rule 'The correction is made on the account's most recent tire invoice of that kind' (posted with no fleet discount, account invoiced without sales tax). argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 229.29. Restored discount: discountable tire price 1,011.72 + 0.00 - disposal 4 x 4.25 = 17.00 - certificate RH-46082417 34.20 x 4 = 136.80 = 857.92 (the price net of the 50.00 instant savings, as tires_purchase_ticket prices the ticket); program tires discount 10% -> 85.79, less 0.00 taken = 85.79 (exactly what correct posting would have given). Make-good: line - the set has 4 tires, so mounting and balancing 4 x 29.00 = 116.00 is credited back; repeat-error credit 10.00 (one pricing correction, 2026-02-20, booked before today in the last twelve months); road hazard program credit 7.50 (six allowances in twenty-four months); tire volume credit 10.00 (seven tire invoices in twelve months). 85.79 + 143.50 = 229.29, within the limit of 1,011.72 (the invoice amount less the credit memos and early-pay discounts already on it, applied last) and the 250.00 desk limit.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.statement_month: Value '2026-09'. Basis: rule 'The late charge for a statement month is assessed on the last day of that month'; frozen_time is 2026-09-30, the last day of September; docstring 'the month-end statement the charge belongs to, written YYYY-MM'. Uniqueness: no other month ends today and no 2026-09 late charge exists.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 12.75. Past-due balance: invoices due before 2026-09-30 plus the two late charges, less every remittance, discount and credit memo, less the 19.00 under open dispute; every older invoice is settled, so it equals 612.40 + 915.92 + 1,011.72 + 49.00 - 229.29 - 153.99 - 19.00 = 2,186.76. Rate = 1.50 - 0.25 (balance 2,764.61 no more than a quarter of 50,000.00) - 0.25 (4,398.40 remitted less than one whole month before the day the charge is assessed, 2026-09-30) - 0.10 (29,110.60 invoiced in twelve months) - 0.10 (33 remittance entries in twelve months) = 0.80. Seasoned account (88 months, one late charge): balance the rate applies to = 1,000.00 + 1,186.76 / 2 = 1,593.38; 1,593.38 x 0.80% = 12.747 -> 12.75, above the 5.00 minimum.
